title: Orthogonal trajectories and eliminating a family parameter
terms: orthogonal trajectory; orthogonal family; negative reciprocal slope; parameter elimina- tion; tangent direction.

exposition.text:
Two curve families are orthogonal trajectories if their tangent lines are perpendicular at ev-
′ ′
ery regular intersection. If one family has slope field y = F(x, y), its orthogonal field is y =
−1/F(x, y) where both finite slopes are defined. Horizontal and vertical tangents must be han-
dled by tangent directions rather than a reciprocal formula with division by zero.
Starting from an implicit family G(x, y, c) = 0, differentiate with respect to x and eliminate the
parameter c using the original equation. Only then take the negative reciprocal and solve the
resulting ODE. The parameter must not remain in a slope field intended to describe the entire
family. Singular intersections may require separate treatment.
For level families F = C and G = K with nonzero gradients, checking ∇F · ∇G = 0 directly
verifies orthogonality. A proposed family may have two different tangents at one point from
different members; then no curve through that point can be perpendicular to both unless those
tangents are parallel. Parameter elimination need not produce a single-valued slope field.

solution.text:

Differentiate y = cx and eliminate c to get y = 2y/x. The orthogonal slope is −x/(2y).

Thus 2y dy = −x dx, which integrates to y = −x /2 + C, or x + 2y = C.

question.text:
2 2
Which family is orthogonal to x − y = C at every regular intersection away from the origin?
2 2 2 2
(A) x + y = K (B) xy = K (C) x − y = K (D) x + 2y = K (E) y/x = K

solution.text:
The normal to the first family is (2x, −2y), and the normal to xy = K is (y, x). Their
dot product is 2xy − 2xy = 0. Rotating both normals by a right angle preserves their
dot product, so the tangent directions are also perpendicular. This checks orthogonality
directly without solving a slope ODE.

question.text:
2 2
Which is the complete family of orthogonal trajectories to x + y = C > 0 in the punctured
plane?
(A) All circles centered at the origin
(B) Only the nonvertical lines y = kx
(C) All radial lines, including the vertical line, with components separated at the omitted origin
(D) All horizontal lines
2
(E) All parabolas y = kx

solution.text:
Circle tangents are perpendicular to the radial vector (x, y), so an orthogonal trajectory
has radial tangent direction and constant polar angle. Its components are rays along lines
through the origin. The vertical line is essential; expressing everything as y(x) can omit it
when taking reciprocal slopes.

question.text:
2
Two members of y = cx + c pass through (0, 1). Which tangent direction at that point is
perpendicular to both members?
(A) Slope 1
(B) Slope −1
(C) Slope 0
(D) Vertical
(E) No nonzero tangent direction has this property.

solution.text:
2
At (0, 1) the parameter must satisfy c = 1, so the two members have slopes 1 and −1. A
perpendicular direction to one has slope −1, while a perpendicular direction to the other
has slope 1. No single nonzero direction satisfies both. Eliminating a family parameter can
give multiple slope branches rather than one direction field.
